Model internals

Inside the Random Forest

Trained on hand–labeled water samples, tested on pixels it never saw. Dense blooms are the hardest class to separate from a diffuse one — the confusion runs almost entirely in that direction.

Confusion matrix · test set

Rows = actual class · columns = predicted class

Feature importance by Sentinel-2 band

The red-edge bands (5, 7) and SWIR1 dominate — exactly the region of the spectrum where chlorophyll absorption and canopy-like algal scattering show up, ahead of the visible bands the eye would rely on.

The basin

Ten reservoirs, one province

Río Tercero alone holds nearly a third of the mapped surface water. Los Molinos — today’s case study — is the second largest.

Surface area from the unified reservoir polygon layer, EPSG:32720.

Method

Sentinel-2 L2A surface reflectance, 10 bands at 20 m, clipped to each reservoir polygon. A Random Forest (200 trees, max depth 12) is trained on hand-drawn regions of interest and validated on a held-out 25% split. This is a research pipeline, not an operational water-quality service — treat the diffuse/dense boundary as a judgment call, not a hard physical threshold.

Source

Sentinel-2 L2A, Copernicus / ESA, via the AWS Earth Search STAC catalog.
Reservoir boundaries: unified polygon layer, prov. of Córdoba.
